subject: general
question: In a redox displacement reaction, if element X loses electrons and element Y gains electrons, then:

options.text: X is oxidised and Y is reduced
X is reduced and Y is oxidised

solution:
The correct answer is __**X is oxidised and Y is reduced**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxidation** is defined as the process involving the **loss of electrons** by a molecule, atom, or ion during a chemical reaction. When element **X** loses electrons, its **oxidation state increases**, and it is said to be **oxidised**.
 
• **Reduction** is the chemical process where a substance **gains electrons**. In the given scenario, element **Y** gains electrons, leading to a **decrease in its oxidation state**, meaning **Y** is **reduced**.
 
• A **Redox reaction** (Reduction-Oxidation) is a type of chemical reaction that involves a **transfer of electrons** between two species. It consists of two **half-reactions** occurring simultaneously: one species undergoes oxidation while the other undergoes reduction.
 
• In a **displacement reaction**, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. This movement of elements is fundamentally driven by the **transfer of electrons**, making most displacement reactions **redox** in nature.
 
• The relationship between the two elements is reciprocal: the electrons lost by **X** are the same electrons gained by **Y**. Therefore, **X** is oxidised and **Y** is reduced.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is X is oxidised and Y is reduced**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reducing Agent (Reductant):**
 
 
• A **reducing agent** is a substance that **donates electrons** to another substance in a redox reaction.
 
• Since element **X** loses electrons to facilitate the reduction of **Y**, **X** acts as the **reducing agent**.
 
• Reducing agents are typically metals or substances with low **electronegativity**.
 
 
 
• **Oxidizing Agent (Oxidant):**
 
 
• An **oxidizing agent** is a substance that **accepts electrons** from another substance.
 
• In this reaction, **Y** gains electrons from **X**, thereby causing **X** to be oxidised; hence, **Y** is the **oxidizing agent**.
 
• Common oxidizing agents include **Oxygen**, **Halogens**, and concentrated acids.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation Number (Oxidation State):**
 
 
• This is a **numerical value** assigned to an atom representing the number of electrons lost or gained.
 
• For **X**, the **oxidation number** becomes more **positive**. For **Y**, the **oxidation number** becomes more **negative** or less positive.
 
• In **elemental form**, the oxidation state of any atom is **0**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mnemonics for Memory:**
 
 
• **OIL RIG**: This stands for **Oxidation Is Loss** and **Reduction Is Gain** (of electrons). This is the most common way to remember the electronic concept of redox.
 
• **LEO says GER**: This stands for **Lose Electrons Oxidation** and **Gain Electrons Reduction**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Displacement:**
 
 
• **Single Displacement**: A more active metal displaces a less active metal ion from a solution, such as **Zinc (Zn)** reacting with **Copper Sulfate (CuSO4)**. In this, **Zn** loses **2** electrons (oxidized) and **Cu2+** gains **2** electrons (reduced).
 
• **Double Displacement**: These are generally **not redox reactions** because they involve the exchange of ions without a change in the oxidation state of the atoms.
 
 
 
• **Electrochemical Series:**
 
 
• The ability of element **X** to displace **Y** depends on their relative positions in the **Activity Series**.
 
• An element higher in the series has a **higher oxidation potential** and can easily lose electrons to reduce elements lower in the series.
 
 
</ul
